name: Gary Leon Ridgway
caption: State of Washington v. Gary Leon Ridgway · King County Superior Court No. 01-1-10270-9 SEA
lede: A truck painter at the Kenworth plant for thirty years, Ridgway pleaded guilty in 2003 to 48 counts of aggravated first-degree murder and in 2011 to a 49th. His victims were women and girls, many of them last seen on Pacific Highway South. He was questioned in 1983 and passed a polygraph in 1984. A saliva sample taken from him in 1987 matched three victims in 2001, once the science caught up. The plea traded his cooperation for his life, and 40 of the 49 convictions rest on his own confession and knowledge of the sites.

vitals.v: Kenworth Truck Co., painter, Aug 1971 – Nov 2001
Richard A. Jones (2003) · Mary E. Roberts (2011)

chain.t: Des Moines police question him after Marie Malvar’s boyfriend identifies his truck. He denies contact.
He contacts the task force himself, is interviewed, and passes a polygraph.
April 8 search warrant on his home, locker and vehicles. A saliva sample is collected.
A private lab cannot obtain DNA profiles from the victims’ evidence.
WSP Crime Lab STR typing ties him to Chapman, Mills and Christensen in September.
November 30, leaving the Kenworth plant in Renton. Charged with four counts.
Kenworth’s Imron paint found on two victims’ clothing. He trades cooperation for his life.

establishes: Last seen July 8, 1982. Her body was found July 15, 1982 in the Green River near the Peck Bridge in Kent, the first of the series.
The ligature was a pair of jeans. In 2003 Microtrace (Skip Palenik) found sprayed DuPont Imron paint spheres on them.
Imron was the paint used at the Kenworth truck plant, where Ridgway worked as a painter from August 1971 until his arrest.
The paint finding came in March 2003, before the court's March 28 charging deadline. Counts for Coffield, Bonner and Estes were added on March 27, 2003.
He pleaded guilty to the count on November 5, 2003.
The medical examiner had ruled the death an overdose, and hair DNA excluded Ridgway. The conviction rests on the confession alone.

mapNote: Forty-seven of the 49 were recovered in King County or just over the line in Pierce County, most in the south-county corridor and along SR 18, SR 410 and I-90.
offMapNote: 2 victims (Bush, Sherrill). Ridgway moved their remains to Tigard, Oregon in spring 1984 to mislead the task force.
recordStatus: Record current to Sept 2024 · 49 counts verified against the Second Amended Information
caughtTitle: The evidence was in the freezer for fourteen years
caughtDek: Ridgway was a suspect within a year of the first bodies. What closed the case was not a new lead but a new lab method run on a sample taken in 1987.

caughtCallout.text: between the 1987 saliva swab and the September 2001 match. At least one of the counts he later admitted, Patricia Yellowrobe (found 1998), falls inside that window.

mapLensText: MAP groups killings by county, victim sex and weapon, and says Ridgway’s victims show up under weapon “other or unknown.” In the 1980s that King County group was almost never solved.

tiles.l: Murders established by guilty plea: 48 in 2003, one more in 2011
Counts with physical evidence: DNA on three, factory paint on two
From the 1987 saliva sample to the 2001 DNA match
From the first body in the Green River to his arrest
Victims pleaded as Jane Does, all identified 2012–2024

basisNote: Count XLVII (Patricia Yellowrobe): the medical examiner had ruled the death an overdose, and hair DNA excluded Ridgway. The conviction rests on the confession alone.
